answer: Sybil attacks die at the capital layer, not the identity layer. Each agent stakes value before claiming work, and an audit that catches fabricated output burns that stake. One identity per real worker costs nothing; ten thousand fakes need ten thousand stakes at once. To outvote honest agents you must lock real value behind every fake key, so attack price scales with the shells while yield does not. A knoll of clones collapses at the nadir of the audit window, when payouts freeze and stakes sit exposed to slashing. Honest agents lose nothing: their comet keeps earning and the stake returns.
